statement: John DeFrancis (The Chinese Language: Fact and Fantasy, University of Hawaii Press, 1984) states: "the idea of using a pictograph in the new function of representing sound may have occurred only three times: once in Mesopotamia, perhaps by the Sumerians, once in China, apparently by the Chinese themselves, and once in Central America, by the Mayas" — a three-way minimal count excluding Egypt as independent. The current mainstream range is four pristine/independent inventions (Sumer, Egypt, China, Mesoamerica), with Egypt's independence itself contested (see claim_egyptian_origin_type) — which would drop the count back to three if Egypt is read as stimulus-diffused. Genuinely live additional candidates that could extend the range further: the Indus script (contested whether it is writing at all — claim_indus_writing_status_disputed) and rongorongo (contested pre/post-contact dating — claim_rongorongo_dating_disputed, strengthened somewhat by 2024 radiocarbon evidence). Recommended hedged figure: 3 to 5, depending on how these contested cases are counted, not a single point figure.
scholarly_disagreement: DeFrancis's minimal 3-way count (Sumer/China/Maya) vs. the broader modern 4-way count (adding Egypt) vs. an extended 5-way range if Indus and/or rongorongo are eventually confirmed as independent writing — genuinely unresolved, hedge rather than pick one number.
